sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026 [2025]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press (LSP 526). 620 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Pukaunu-specific statement. Pukaunu appears on p. 100 (map), p. 137 fn. 22 (lexical similarity 44% Painara-Pukaunu, 41% Sika-Pukaunu, from Keraf 1978: 448), p. 139 Table 3.39 (five forms), p. 166 (classification: 'Pukaunu [---]' as the first split within West Lamaholot) and p. 731 (language table: 'Pukaunu --- puka1244 -8.43 122.71 Fricke 2019, Keraf 1978'). Only an areal remark on p. 115: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables.'

sources.citation: Michels, Jonathan. 2017. A sketch of Western Lamaholot (cross-dialectal). Leiden RMA thesis.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.2.1 p. 25, generic: 'Stress in Lamaholot is not usually contrastive. The general rule is that stress is on the penultimate syllable, but even neighbouring dialects may vary in the details.' Dialects discussed are Lewotobi, Lewoingu, Lewolema, Ile Mandiri, Solor (Pamakayo), Horowura; Pukaunu/Muhang not mentioned.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record puka1244 'Pukaunu' (alias Muhang) with its six linked references (Keraf 1978; Fricke 2019; Grimes & Edwards 2025; Sugono 2008 Bahasa dan peta bahasa di Indonesia; Sugono et al. 2002 Kosakata Dasar Swadesh.; Needham 1985).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Classification note: 'E16-E28 includes Pukaunu (aka Muhang) in its Lamaholot [slp] entry. However, the language of Pukaunu is far too distant to be intelligible to other (West) Lamaholot varieties (Keraf 1978: 14-15, 448) and thus merits its own entry.' No descriptive (grammar/sketch/phonology) reference is attached.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L.A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544 (Leiden PhD). Utrecht: LOT. xxiii+573 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing about Pukaunu. 'Pukaunu'/'Muhang' occur only on p. 68 (Table 3.20, five Keraf nouns), p. 157 with fn. 4 ('The Western Lamaholot varieties in the Sikka regency are called Muhang and are largely undescribed. [fn 4] Most likely the variety Keraf (1978a) labels as Pukaunu, located in the western edge of the Flores Timur regency, is similar or identical to Muhang.') and p. 162 (sample table: 'pk - Pukaunu Keraf 1978b'). The stress section 3.2.5 (pp. 49-50: penultimate unless penult is schwa) is the grammar of Central Lembata [levu1239] only.

sources.citation: Nagaya, Naonori. 2010. A phonological sketch of Lewotobi Lamaholot. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 5: 157-195 (author preprint). [nearest described Western Lamaholot neighbour, lewo1244; NOT Pukaunu]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: For Lewotobi only: 'Stress in Lewotobi Lamaholot regularly falls on the penultimate syllable of a word, unless the word is monosyllabic' (sec. 4); enclitics shift stress rightwards. Different languoid; not usable as a Pukaunu statement.

sources.citation: Kaiping, Gereon, Owen Edwards & Marian Klamer (eds.). LexiRumah (CLDF), lect lama1277-pukau 'Pukaunu Lamaholot' (Kecamatan Talibura, Kabupaten Sikka; glottocode puka1244; source keraf1978), 198 forms.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wordlist only; 0 of 198 Pukaunu forms carry a stress mark (7 carry a length mark), so Keraf's list gives no stress information.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna. 2014. Topics in the grammar of Hewa: a variety of Sika in eastern Flores, Indonesia. Leiden MA thesis / LINCOM (Hewa is the Sika variety of the same Talibura area, adjacent to Muhang).

sources.note: The only primary data on Pukaunu ever published; the sole source behind Glottolog's, Fricke's, Grimes & Edwards' and LexiRumah's Pukaunu entries. A wordlist, so a stress statement is unlikely, but pp. 14-15 might carry a phonetic remark, and the printed list could carry stress/accent diacritics lost in digitisation.
